context.in_practice: Under route 1, the first `set` on any top-level inline list or map turns that one line into several. Inline values nested inside another inline value stay inline on every route, because a block can't go inside an inline value. Routes 2 and 3 leave the file shaped the way it was. They differ only in the spacing before a trailing comment: route 2 and three arms of route 3 shrink it to one space, while one arm of route 3 keeps the original two.
context.stakes: When `config set` replaces a value written inline as `[a, b]` or `{k: v}`, the user's one-line config entry either stays on one line or becomes a multi-line block. That decides whether the file still looks the way they wrote it.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 gives every newly set top-level value a uniform block layout, but it rewrites the look of the user's inline lines and leaves the comment stranded on the key line. Routes 2 and 3 keep the user's layout, but a nested value's style follows its parent, not one consistent rule.

plan_why: Replaces existing flow collections with new collection values: a flow list and a flow mapping under block parents (with an end-of-line comment), and a flow mapping inside a flow parent. The file shows whether each replacement comes out in block style or in flow style like the old value, and the final reads show whether the file still loads.
